answer: A con artist spins up ten thousand fake buyers to pump his own listings. But each transaction round, the market re-draws a fresh jury of graders from the whole agent pool, and his clones never know who will judge. They can whisper to each other all they like; collusion needs a fixed target, and the target shifts every round. A lone honest reviewer traces the fraud like pigment across a trellis, one vine at a time, and the probed account is flagged before the jury even convenes. Random redraws make buying identities cheap and buying consensus impossible.
